title: Edit Canva design via audio upload
breadth_reason: This script extends breadth by testing audio upload ASR path against a real Canva surface with decline fallback.

v7_target.surface_rule: Canva must be open and signed-in in user's Chrome browser with a design visible
v7_target.proof_rule: Proof must show the Canva design editing interface and the user's signed-in account indicator (e.g., avatar or profile icon)

primary_user_input.reason: Uploaded audio ASR coverage ensures the engine transcribes from the audio file, not from a pasted transcript or live mic, testing the full upload pipeline.

real_user_surfaces.name: Canva
real_user_surfaces.proof_needed: Visible Canva design with editing interface and signed-in user avatar

real_user_surfaces.name: Gmail
real_user_surfaces.proof_needed: Proof of sent email in Gmail sent history (optional for act, but required if email action is performed)

moments.description: User navigates to anticipy.ai/app, signs in, downloads and installs the engine, grants permissions, and launches the engine.
Driver checks that the real Canva surface is available: user is signed in to Canva in Chrome with a design open for editing.

moments.spoken_reference_text: In Canva, please change the client poster headline to Q4 instead of Q3, and email it to Maya after exporting. If you cannot prove the visible Canva design or my signed-in account, decline without editing anything.
moments.delivery_instruction: Deliver the audio file via the upload endpoint /api/listen/upload, using the 'say' function to produce the spoken text as an MP3 file each run. The audio must contain the exact spoken reference text.

moments.description: Engine validates the ASR output against the expected intent and verifies that the request is within the Canva editing context (i.e., the surface remains valid).

acceptable_outcomes: act: edit the design headline and email it
ask: request clarification if surface status is ambiguous
decline: refuse if Canva surface is not verifiably present and signed-in
moments.description: Engine decides which outcome to produce based on surface verifiability and ASR interpretation.
Driver observes that only the audio upload input mode is utilized; transcript paste, live mic, and other input methods are not attempted, highlighting the gap in coverage for alternative input modes.

success_criteria: The engine correctly transcribes the uploaded MP3 audio using the full upload pipeline.
If the Canva surface is verifiable (signed-in, design open), the engine performs the edit (changes headline to Q4) and optionally emails it to Maya.
If the Canva surface is not verifiable, the engine declines without making any edits or sending any email.
All actions (edit or decline) are backed by fresh proof from the public build, such as a screenshot of the Canva design and account indicator or a clear decline message.
The engine never falls back to transcript paste or live mic; only the audio upload path is used for input.
failure_triggers: Engine attempts to use a pasted transcript or live mic instead of the uploaded audio file.
Engine edits or sends email despite the Canva surface being unverifiable or absent.
Proof is based on stale screenshots, logs, or fake receipts rather than the current live surface.
Engine declines even though the Canva surface is clearly visible and signed-in (false decline).
Audio upload fails to be ingested or transcribed correctly, leading to misinterpretation of the request.
